thread:
adrian: Hey folks — PM wants a small prototype of org-scoped operational dashboards for customers. Requirements: per-customer quota burn, routing policy breakdown (which model/variant served), and "noisy neighbor" signals. Prototype due next Wed. What can runtime + infra realistically provide without big perf hits? @jordan @selene

maya: UI questions: do they want a full per-org console page or a set of panels that can be filtered by org? Also need RBAC note — only account admins should see org scope. :lock:

jordan: Runtime notes (quick list):
- cheap to emit per-request labels: org_hash, model, variant, route_tag, cache_hit (0/1)
- metrics we can already produce: request_latency_ms (histogram), tokens_in/out (counters), queue_time_ms, batch_size (gauge), batch_wait_ms
- expensive: adding org_hash to high-cardinality histograms (prometheus blows up). prefer emitting per-org *counters* to a tenant-metrics pipeline and aggregated histograms at ingest.
- can emit a lightweight event to Kafka: topic=tenant.metrics.v1 with schema (org_hash, timestamp, model, latency_ms, tokens, cache_hit, route) — small JSON per request or sampled 1/10.
- also can periodically emit tenant-level rollups from each worker (1m window): requests_total, tokens_total, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, batch_size_avg.

selene: Infra constraints + proposal:
- we can ingest runtime events into our metrics pipeline (Kafka -> stream processor -> metrics backend) and pre-aggregate per-org windows to avoid cardinality blowup.
- infra will provide node/GPU level metrics (gpu_util, memory_pressure, gpu_temperature, preempt_count) and a node->tenant mapping for active allocations.
- noisy-neighbor signals we can synthesize: sudden_request_spike_rate(org), tail_latency_ratio(org) = p99/p50, sustained_gpu_fairness_drop(org) (measured via per-tenant share of GPU cycles).
- retention/SCOPING: tenant rollups stored for 90d, raw events for 7d. RBAC enforced at query layer (console will call metrics API with org-scoped token).

maya: For the Console UX: we need these panels at minimum: 1) "Org Overview" (quota burn, requests/min, tokens/min, avg latency), 2) "Routing" (pie by model/variant + time series of fallback events), 3) "Noisy neighbor" (spikes, tail ratios, gpu_share). Charts should allow baseline comparisons (last 1h vs prior 1h). Also need an alert template for "org noisy neighbor score > threshold" and a link to open support ticket.

adrian: Good. Actionable proposal:
- Runtime (jordan): implement tenant.metrics.v1 event + per-worker 1m rollup emission. Add a runtime flag `emit_org_label` (default off) to guard prometheus labels. Use `org_hash` not raw org id. Deadline: Tue EOW for a canary.
- Infra (selene): build consumer that aggregates tenant.metrics.v1 into per-org rollups and push to metrics store + provide dashboard skeleton (Grafana/Console). Deadline: Thu next week.
- Console (maya): wire up org dropdown, RBAC checks, and the three starter panels. Wire alerting template. Deadline: next Wed (prototype).

jordan: Sounds fine. Implementation notes: we'll sample full events (1/20 by default) and emit rollups every 60s. Example rollup payload (one line): `{"org_hash":"<hex>","ts":1769543210,"requests":42,"tokens":12345,"avg_latency_ms":85.2,"p95_ms":210}`. We'll gzip+snappy compress and send to tenant.metrics.v1.

selene: Security note: use org_hash salted with a cluster secret (rotating) so no reversible mapping. Also ensure metrics pipeline drops any free-text fields (e.g., prompt) — only structured routing/model ids allowed.

jordan: We'll implement hashing in runtime. Also adding `emit_org_label` to prometheus exporter but keep it off for now. We'll log a single debug line when enabled to help infra detect cardinality issues.

adrian: Owner tags: jordan -> runtime change (PR + canary), selene -> aggregator + dashboard skeleton, maya -> console wiring + alert template. I'll own the cross-team PR and the product acceptance criteria.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary job queued: infra/metrics-ingestor v2 -> namespace=staging, runtime/metrics-producer v1.3 -> rolling-canary 5%

adrian: Thanks. One more: selene, do you need any sample data from prod to validate noisy-neighbor heuristics?

selene: Yes please — if runtime can enable a 1-hour sampling window with full events (not rollups) for a single org we pick, we can run heuristics offline. Can be short-lived and then disabled.

jordan: Ok I'll coordinate a 1-hour sample for org_hash="sample-org-xxxx" tomorrow 10:00 UTC and then revert. Will post a short PR and config toggle.

adrian: Great — that's enough to get the prototype moving. Will follow up with ticket IDs. :rocket:
